  RFC8836-2-8b partial -> tested and RFC8836-2-9 missing -> partial (stale notes: `a=rtcp-rsize`
  is negotiated and used; datagrams are DSCP-marked, the estimator does not use the marking).
  Tests and audit only.
- test-env interop: the two browser loss-recovery cells ("loss recovery: NACK and RTX repair a
  browser's video under netem" and "... the browser's SSRCs unsignalled ...") check, before
  their loss checks, the payload types Rust received against the browser's own offer and the
  answer (`common.mjs unlessOffFormat`). Media on a payload type the offer does not have fails
  the cell with that payload type, its packet count, both descriptions' video format lines and
  what the browser says it sends with (`Interop.codecView`: RTCRtpSendParameters.codecs,
  outbound-rtp codecId), and says whether it is a format the answer added (RFC 9429 section
  5.3.1, allowed by RFC 3264 section 7, not the format the cell measures) or one the answer
  does not have either (RFC 3264 section 7; the engine's `unnegotiatedPayloadTypeRtp` count),
  instead of an unexplained "span 0". For WebKit, seen switching its VP8 sender to the
  answer's VP9 on 98 in 6 of 240 runs, it is recorded as a `known-browser-defect` annotation
  and the cell runs once more, on that evidence only; the second attempt is checked in full (a
  second switch fails the cell, named). Every attempt logs its payload types. The interop
  peer's report carries `unnegotiatedPayloadTypeRtp`; a failed cell's descriptions are saved
  under `failed-cell-sdp/` in the artifacts; the matrix and gate show a pass after such a
  retry. "chrome profile: audio and video both ways" logs the same payload types and names such
  a switch as its failure (no retry there).
- **RFC 10079, the updated SFrame cipher suites registry, is audited and its registry columns
  tested** (`docs/conformance/audit/rfc10079.md`; `conf/sframe-3-rfc10079-cipher-suite-registry`;
  test, documentation and audit only, no code change). `rtci-sframe` already had the AES-256-CTR
  with HMAC-SHA512 suites 0x0006 to 0x0008 from the RFC's draft; their vectors are byte for byte
  those of RFC 10079 Appendix A.2 (the RFC's Appendix A.1 gives no AEAD-only vectors). New test
  `rtci-sframe/src/context_test.rs::cipher_suites_have_the_registry_columns_of_rfc10079` (`Nh`,
  `Nka`, `Nk`, `Nn`, `Nt` of Tables 1 and 2 for all eight suites); the crate's references move
  from draft-barnes-sframe-iana-256 to RFC 10079.
- **Calls whose audio and video do not start in the same instant**
  (`conf/probe-2-staggered-start-tests`; tests only, no engine change). Every two-peer call of
  the capacity world (`tests/capacity_common`) and every instrument cell wrote its first audio
  and video frames in the same instant, so none ever sent a call's first packet before the
  video had: the window of the probe-1 fix above, which only an interceptor-level test reached.
  `Setup::start_order` (audio or video first by N ms; the same instant by default, with the
  old arithmetic exactly; byte-identical rows not yet shown) and an optional seventh part of an instrument cell's name (`aN`, `vN`).
  New `tests/probe_start_order_rtc2rtc.rs`, two peer connections on an open link, both peers
  held to 1 Mbit/s and the 2.5 Mbit/s maximum (RFC 8836 section 2, requirement 4):
  audio first by 10 and 25 ms in the chains without a pacer (1 Mbit/s after 1.07 s with the
  probe-1 fix, never in the 5 s on 0.2.0, which stays at 450 kbit/s) and with the pacer
  (0.37 s, either engine); video first by 10 ms in every chain (0.27 to 0.37 s, either
  engine); and an audio-only call that gains video by renegotiation after 3 s. That last one
  FAILS in every chain, with the pacer too, on 0.2.0 and with the probe-1 fix alike: no
  cluster is ever carried after the video starts (no padding; 460 to 490 kbit/s six seconds
  later, the controller's 8 % a second). Its three tests fail until `probe-3`, which also
  shortens the audio-first start-up (1.07 s against 0.37 s when the video sends first).
- **Browser cells for `max-bundle` with audio, video and a data channel**
  (`conf/bundle-3-max-bundle-browser-cells`, `conf/bundle-4-browser-form-of-bundle-only-sections`; `scripts/test-env/interop/scenarios.spec.mjs`,
  `peer.js`, `examples/interop-peer`; test harness only, no engine change; RFC 9429 sections
  4.1.1, 5.2.1 and 5.3.1, RFC 9143 sections 7.2 and 13, RFC 8841 section 5.1). The two
  regressions above went out in 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 because the browser matrix had `bundlePolicy`
  cells only for `max-compat` and `balanced`, and browsers default to `balanced`, so no browser
  ever sent the engine a bundle-only data section or answered one. Six cells, in Chromium,
  Firefox and WebKit: the browser offers under `bundlePolicy: "max-bundle"` and Rust answers,
  Rust offers under `RTCBundlePolicy::MaxBundle` and the browser answers, each with the channel
  created after the tracks and before them (the data section first in Chromium's offer; that
  cell negotiates Cryptex as well), and from either initial offer a renegotiation from each side
  (the browser offers again, then Rust offers a second channel). Each cell asserts the answer
  accepts every section (a port, no `a=bundle-only`, one group naming every mid, the data
  section's `a=sctp-port`), the channel opens and carries messages both ways and never closes,
  the SCTP association is connected on both sides with the same `a=sctp-port` throughout, audio
  and video flow, and, for Rust's offer, the engine's must-bundle form (the first section with a
  port, every other port zero and `a=bundle-only`, the data section last). What the browser
  wrote is recorded as the `max-bundle-offer` / `max-bundle-answer` annotation, and the
  browsers' descriptions are kept as `browser-sdp/*.sdp` artifacts (`recordDescriptions`). The
  interop peer takes `?bundle_policy=<name>` (`RTCConfigurationBuilder::with_bundle_policy`),
  `request-offer`'s `"data_channel": "before" | "after"` with `"tracks"`, and reports
  `dcReceived` (messages received on every channel). Rust's offers in these cells use the
  `Chrome` profile (`with_bundle_only_sections_in_browser_form`, above); a
  seventh cell offers in the default profile's RFC 9143 form and records each browser's refusal
  as na-browser with the browser's own error text, failing on any other outcome than a refusal
  for the missing `a=rtcp-mux` or a full pass. `scripts/test-env/hosted-cell.sh` makes `opus.ogg`
  as the image does and runs Firefox as the runner's user (from `conf/ci-hosted-cell-firefox`).
  `tests/jsep_default_offers_pinned.rs` pins the default initial offers (default policy,
  `max-bundle`, `must-bundle`, `max-compat`; normalized) in `tests/fixtures/engine-offers/`,
  written by the test on the code before the setting (bundle-3, run 45911540683): the default
  form of the bundle-only sections is unchanged byte for byte.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-11-26

The second release under the `rtci` names. Since 0.1.0: trains 21 to 34 of the
clause-by-clause conformance work (the audit's open MUST rows down to 7, none a violation, and
no SHOULD row marked violated), and defaults of the congestion and repair path under which, in
the capacity instrument's measured cells (`tests/capacity_instrument.rs`, figures in
`docs/performance.md`), a call through a sudden capacity drop, an outage or a slow path keeps a
recent picture and its audio.

- **Breaking changes** (below, each with its migration): the NACK responder declines repairs
  that cannot be useful and gives a video stream up after a halving of the target; the default
  pacer discards queued video at a collapse; `SampleBuilder` gives a gap up after 300 ms; the
  RTP circuit breaker restarts a ceased flow; a ULPFEC packet in a RED stream reaches the
  application without a payload; new public fields on several configuration structs; the stream
  driver runs on an injected async runtime and loses some auto traits.
- **Security**: key material in rtci-dtls, rtci-srtp and rtci-crypto is erased when no longer
  needed, with both providers; `Display` and `Debug` no longer print keys.
- **Known limits** (below): both directions capped at once, a deep queue on the path, copies of
  SRTP keys in the dead stack frames of the thread that built the context, the `Chrome`
  profile's picture after a collapse, and the recovery after a deep cap without the opt-in
  probing.
- The engine's STUN SOFTWARE text is `rtci-ice 0.2.0`, 4 bytes shorter than master's
  `rtci-ice 0.2.0-dev`: every STUN packet is 4 bytes shorter, which re-draws the capacity
  instrument's seeds (performance ledger row `release-0.2.0`).

### Security

- **Key material left in freed memory by rtci-dtls, rtci-srtp and rtci-crypto is now erased**
  (`conf/zeroize-1-dtls-srtp-key-erasure`; RFC 5246 section 8.1, RFC 8446 section 7.1, RFC 3711
  section 9.3, RFC 7714 section 13.1; docs/key-erasure.md). In 0.1.0 (and on master until this
  change) these stayed in heap memory after it was freed, until the allocator reused it:
  DTLS 1.2: the PRF (`prf_p_hash`) built its output and intermediate values in plain vectors, so
  the master secret, the key block (every record key and IV) and the DTLS-SRTP exporter output
  (the SRTP master keys and salts) were left behind; `State` held the master and premaster
  secrets in plain vectors (replaced or dropped without erasure; the ECDHE shared secret was
  unwrapped from its `SecretVec`); a PSK returned by the application's callback was not erased;
  `EncryptionKeys` printed every key through `Display` and `Debug`; the record ciphers' write
  IVs were plain; the serialized `State` and ticket plaintexts left copies while being built;
  the previous cookie secret of an endpoint (after a rotation) was never erased, and cookie
  secrets, like ticket keys and the DTLS 1.3 HelloRetryRequest cookie secret, stayed in the
  buffered generator's output buffer.
  DTLS 1.3: record IVs held inline in epochs that live in vectors were copied into memory the
  vectors freed. SRTP and DTLS with the ring provider: the RustCrypto HMAC-SHA1 states (the
  AES-CM and NULL profiles' authentication keys, the AES-CBC suite's MAC keys) were not erased;
  RustCrypto `aes` was built without `zeroize`, so AES-CBC and AES-CCM key schedules and the
  per-packet AES-CM ones were not erased. With the ring provider, ring's own key objects were
  freed as they were: the SRTP AES-GCM session keys and every AES round key
  (`ring::aead::LessSafeKey`), the DTLS record keys of the AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 suites,
  the DTLS 1.3 record-number keys (`aead::quic::HeaderProtectionKey`) and the HMAC-SHA-2 states
  of the PRF, HKDF and cookie keys (`hmac::Key`); the ECDHE private key, left in the freed
  key-exchange object (`agreement::EphemeralPrivateKey`), and the certificate's Ed25519 and
  ECDSA P-256 key pairs. Key schedules and shared secrets also left copies in
  dead stack frames that later moves carried into heap padding. All of these are now erased:
  `SecretVec` everywhere (it implements `Zeroize` and `ZeroizeOnDrop`), structs that hold keys
  derive both, buffers are sized up front, `aes`/`ctr` are built with `zeroize`, the HMAC-SHA1
  state is overwritten on drop, ring's key objects live in an allocation of the provider's own
  that is overwritten after ring has dropped them (`ErasedOnDrop`; ring declines to erase them
  itself, ring issue #15), `crypto::scrub_stack` runs after keyed objects and shared
  secrets are built, and secrets are drawn with the new `RTCRandom::fill_secret` (the built-in
  providers read the operating system for it). Tests: `tests/dtls_secret_erasure.rs` (every
  freed heap block and every block still allocated, all platforms; the whole process on Linux
  outside dead stack frames, see Known limits),
  the DTLS 1.2 exporter test of `tests/dtls_srtp_keying_material_erasure.rs` (was a known
  limit), `with_ring_no_key_*` in `rtci-srtp/tests/key_schedule_erasure.rs` and
  `key_erasure_process_memory.rs` (were the `known_limit_*` tests),
  `rtci-crypto/tests/ring_key_object_erasure.rs` (each ring key object, the ECDHE private key
  drawn from a known seed through the new test-support seam `ring_key_exchange_with_seed`, the
  signing key pairs). What remains: a ring RSA key pair keeps its private limbs in ring's own
  heap allocations (not reachable, not measured); stack copies left while key objects are built
  are scrubbed but not observed by any test (a copy moved onto the stack is not caught), so
  their absence is not guaranteed (docs/key-erasure.md); RFC7714-13.1-3 stays `partial`
  (class E) for that. No wire or handshake behaviour changes. Additions to the API:
  `RTCRandom::fill_secret` (default: `fill`), `crypto::scrub_stack`, `Zeroize`/`ZeroizeOnDrop`
  for `SecretVec` and `SessionKeys`. Cost (`rtci-srtp` and `rtci-dtls` criterion benchmarks
  against master 6939a3e8 on the same runner, run 45660052237; master figures in brackets):
  DTLS record-cipher setup 1.07 µs AES-128-GCM (0.39 µs) and 1.38 µs AES-256-CBC (0.47 µs),
  of which about 0.7 µs is the 32 KiB stack overwrite (`crypto::scrub_stack`, one bulk fill;
  the first form, a volatile write per byte, took 13.8 µs and 22.5 µs, run 45654600978);
  SRTP context setup 1.48 µs AES-CM (1.43 µs) and 1.31 µs AES-128-GCM (1.12 µs: ring's key
  object in an allocation of its own); per packet SRTP AES-CM RTP 1.52 µs / 1.23 µs encrypt /
  decrypt (1.53 / 1.26 µs), RTCP 271 ns / 307 ns (264 / 279 ns), SRTP AES-128-GCM RTP 625 ns
  / 330 ns (627 / 337 ns), DTLS records 258 / 270 ns AES-128-GCM and 3.16 / 2.89 µs
  AES-256-CBC (within 1-4 % of master, faster). That `scrub_stack` still overwrites is
  tested: emptied, or with its fill left unobservable to the optimiser, the DTLS erasure
  tests fail in a release build (the second case cannot be told apart in a debug build,
  where nothing is optimised away).

### Breaking changes

- **interceptor, peer connection** (`conf/nack-11-decline-useless-repairs`): **the NACK
  responder declines repairs that cannot be useful, and asks for a key frame instead.** Two
  rules, on by default in every chain (RFC 8834 section 6.1: "It is not appropriate to
  blindly retransmit RTP packets in response to a NACK. The importance of lost packets and
  the likelihood of them arriving in time to be useful need to be considered"; RFC 4588
  section 7: "If congestion is not kept under control, then retransmission SHOULD NOT be
  used"): (1) a NACK for a packet written more than 2 s ago is not answered
  (`NackResponderBuilder::with_max_repair_age`, `NACK_MAX_REPAIR_AGE`); (2) when the requests
  waiting would take 2 s or more to send at the target and the target has fallen to half or
  less within 2 s, they are given up (`with_repair_backlog_bound`,
  `NACK_REPAIR_BACKLOG_BOUND`). Giving a video stream up forgets everything sent on it so far,
  releases the retransmission reserve at once and asks the application for one key frame of
  it (a PLI with sender SSRC 0 on `poll_read`, `OnKeyFrameRequest`: the pacer's flush has the
  same request); the targets from before a give-up no longer count, so the key frame that
  answers is given up in its turn only if the target halves again. Audio is only declined by
  age. **An `rtx-time` takes the place of the age bound** (RFC 4588 section 8.1: "the maximum
  time a sender will keep an original RTP packet in its buffers available for
  retransmission"): where one is in force for a stream (`NackControl::LocalRtxTime` from the
  session description or the application, `NackResponderBuilder::with_max_packet_age`), a
  packet of the stream is repaired for that long, shorter or longer than 2 s, and past it the
  packet is not retransmitted and nothing else happens, as before (no give-up, no key-frame
  request); the 2 s are the sender's own judgement where no time was set. The `rtx-time` is
  that of the packet's own retransmission format (RFC 4588 section 8.6: a parameter of each
  RTX payload type; with red-2 a RED packet goes under the RTX of `red`), and the same value
  governs all three uses for that packet: the age cut, the 2 s rule and the give-up. So a RED
  packet whose RTX of `red` announces no `rtx-time` falls under the 2 s rule and gives the
  stream up, whatever the media format's RTX announces, and the reverse. A NACK entry that
  would never be answered (a FEC packet in RED on a stream without RTX, a payload type with
  no RTX format on a stream that has RTX) never gives the stream up by its age: the receiver
  is not waiting for a picture because of it (conf/red-2r; tests `rtci-interceptor/tests/
  nack_rtx_red.rs::an_old_red_packet_is_held_to_the_repair_age_when_only_the_media_rtx_announces_a_time`,
  `a_red_packet_is_repaired_for_the_rtx_time_of_the_rtx_of_red_and_a_plain_packet_is_not`,
  `an_old_packet_that_is_never_answered_does_not_give_the_stream_up`,
  `the_backlog_counts_red_packets_at_the_size_of_their_answers`). Ordinary loss at a steady target is repaired as before and asks for
  no key frame. Before, every NACK for a packet still in the 1024-packet buffer was served in
  order: a call without a pacer that met a capacity drop from 2.5 Mbit/s to 300 kbit/s sent
  142 retransmissions (38 dropped again) with its target held at the reserve's floor, now 18
  (16), median target under the cap 229 -> 257 kbit/s (behind a 100 ms queue 142 -> 252); a
  receiver without a bound in time showed a picture 7.5 s old, now 1.1 s; after a 4 s outage
  the default chain resumed later than 2 s in 66 of 200 calls with such a receiver, now in
  none (`docs/capacity-collapse.md`, "The NACK responder": the figures by cell, why 2 s).
  `DefaultInterceptorOptions` has two new public fields, `nack_max_repair_age` and
  `nack_repair_backlog_bound` (a struct literal without `..Default::default()` no longer
  compiles), governed by the behaviour profiles (`nack.max-repair-age`,
  `nack.repair-backlog-bound`: `None` in the `Chrome` profile, whose sender never asks itself
  for a key frame). **`PacerBacklog::Keep` now also switches both rules off** in the default
  interceptor set: the option means "keep and repair everything" (its name is unchanged).
  Migration, for a receiver that plays strictly in order and cannot resume at a key frame:
  `options.pacer_backlog = PacerBacklog::Keep`, or on a chain built by hand
  `NackResponderBuilder::with_max_repair_age(None).with_repair_backlog_bound(None)`. An
  application must answer a key-frame request with a key frame, as for a remote PLI. No
  `rtx-time` is announced for the age bound. `DELIVERED_MEMORY` (4 s) is unchanged: under the
  default age bound a packet's memory is unreachable once the packet is 2 s old, and it is
  the bound where a packet is repaired longer (an `rtx-time` over 2 s, the age rule off).
  Known small effect: a give-up does not tell the pacer, so a retransmission of a forgotten
  packet already queued there still leaves (counted in 700 paced calls with 247 give-ups: 3 in
  all, at one give-up). A small cost, accepted: in a chain without a pacer behind a 100 ms
  queue the climb back after the cap is slightly slower (seconds to 1000 kbit/s median
  17.85 -> 18.30, 90th percentile 19.10 -> 20.40, per seed +0.26 +-0.24 s; target 15-25 s after
  the cap 1215 -> 1195 kbit/s; 200 calls), and calls over 20 s go from 3 to 31 of 200 since the
  climb clusters at 17-21 s; with both directions capped the 15-25 s target is 44-66 kbit/s
  lower (not significant) against 89-90 kbit/s more target while the cap holds. Paced chains
  move too on the tree this landed on (train 34 round 7, 58ba8a93, against round 6's rows; the
  branch's own base showed the paced cells identical): the rules decline repairs there as well,
  a declined repair leaving an unusable frame that a key frame answers. Both directions capped
  (`cap/paced/gap300/both/q300/rl0`, 111 of 200 calls move): unusable frames 1.07 -> 2.75 a
  call, key frames 4.9 -> 5.1, target 15-25 s after the cap 1375 -> 1369 kbit/s, against
  retransmissions 4.8 -> 2.7 and an oldest picture 2.49 -> 2.44 s; 5 % loss on the reverse path
  (`cap/paced/gap300/up/q300/rl5`, 107 of 200): target 15-25 s after 1367 -> 1354 kbit/s,
  seconds to 1000 kbit/s 16.44 -> 16.53, a peer outside `connected` at the end 1 -> 2 of 200;
  the 4 s outage (`outage/paced/gap300/up/q300/rl0`, 66 of 200: the calls whose picture the
  restart of probing at a path change had made older) gains: oldest picture 4.76 -> 4.32 s,
  retransmissions 133 -> 36, first picture after the new pair 0.71 -> 0.26 s. The reference
  cells (1000 calls each) and the 100 ms queue are identical; the 1000 ms queue moves in 2 of
  200 (instrument runs 45695138492 / 45695149408 against 45686735759 / 45686744374; the
  merge-point rule holds, nothing flagged). Fixed with it: a probe cluster asked for while
  the responder's buffer is empty (after a give-up or the pacer's flush, before the next
  packet is written) is still padded, under the header of the newest packet the buffer held;
  before, no padding left, and a chain without a pacer stopped probing.
- **peer connection, interceptor, media** (`conf/red-3-fec-sequence-holes`): **a ULPFEC packet
  received in a RED stream is delivered to the application as an RTP packet without a
  payload**, under the payload type of the stream's media, with the FEC packet's sequence
  number and timestamp (`RTCMessage::RtpPacket` with an empty `payload`; the peer connection
  used to drop it). ULPFEC in RED packets of its own (the form browsers send, and the `Chrome`
  behaviour profile's) takes sequence numbers of the media stream, so an application that
  puts frames together saw a missing packet at each of them: a frame of more than five
  packets was never complete, and each hole between frames waited out the gap bound and
  cost a key-frame request. Between two engines of the `Chrome` profile at 2 Mbit/s no
  frame was usable while FEC was sent. Migration: give every packet of the stream to the
  frame assembly, empty ones included (`SampleBuilder::push` and `rtci-video`'s receiver take
  them as present and no media); code that reads `payload[0]` of every packet must skip an
  empty payload. The receive interceptor's emptied packet (`UlpfecRepair`) now has the
  media's payload type instead of the `ulpfec` one (the `ulpfec` one only before any media
  of the stream arrived).
- **interceptor** (`conf/red-3-fec-sequence-holes`): **with `RedPlacement::OwnPacket` the FEC
  packets follow the last packet of a frame** (the one with the marker bit) instead of each
  block's last packet: `UlpfecSendBuilder::with_fec_after_frame`, on by default, as libwebrtc
  places them (`ulpfec_generator.cc:134,157-159` at a222406d). A receiver, libwebrtc's
  included, finds a frame only over consecutive sequence numbers, so a FEC packet inside a
  frame left it incomplete. Each FEC packet protects the same media packets as before; only
  the order on the wire changes (RFC 5109 and RFC 2198 say nothing about it). At most
  `ULPFEC_MAX_HELD_FEC_PACKETS` (128) FEC packets wait for a marker bit. Migration: none for
  video with marker bits; `with_fec_after_frame(false)` restores the old order. The other
  placements and carriages are unchanged.
- **media** (`conf/red-3-fec-sequence-holes`): `SampleBuilder` takes **a packet without a
  payload as present and no media**. It is left out of the sample it lies in (a sample with
  one inside it used to be lost to a depacketizer error); it starts no sample, so a sample
  followed by such packets waits for the next packet with a payload and has its real
  `duration` (it used to come out at once with a duration of zero); between samples it is
  counted in `prev_padding_packets` whatever its timestamp (only one with the last sample's
  timestamp was); and `pop` goes on to the next sample after dropping packets that belong
  to none (it used to return `None` once for each such run). Migration: none needed; code
  that relied on a zero duration to spot padding reads `prev_padding_packets`.
- **interceptor, peer connection** (`conf/flush-1r-backlog-flush-at-collapse`): **the default
  pacer discards queued video when the path's capacity collapses.** When what waits in the
  pacer would take a second or more to leave and the target is half or less of what it was
  when that media was written (or within the last two seconds), the queue and its
  retransmissions are discarded, the NACK responder answers no NACK for what was sent before,
  and the application is asked for a key frame of each video stream (a PLI with sender SSRC 0
  on `poll_read`, `OnKeyFrameRequest`, `OnPacerDiscard`); the source is not paused. Before,
  the source was paused and everything was delivered in order, which left the receiver's
  picture 7.9 s old in the median after a drop from 2.5 Mbit/s to 300 kbit/s; now 1.33 s
  (`docs/capacity-collapse.md`: the texts, the figures by cell, the limits). An application
  must answer a key-frame request with a key frame, and a receiver must bound its wait for a
  missing packet or resume at a key frame (`SampleBuilder` does by default). Migration, for
  a receiver that plays strictly in order: `options.pacer_backlog = PacerBacklog::Keep`, or
  `PacerBuilder::with_backlog(PacerBacklog::Keep)`. `DefaultInterceptorOptions` has a new
  public field, `pacer_backlog`: a struct literal without `..Default::default()` no longer
  compiles.
  Performance: flush-1r
- **media** (`conf/flush-2-receiver-gap-bound`): `SampleBuilder` gives a gap up by default.
  A builder of a video format (`Depacketizer::has_key_frames`: VP8, VP9, AV1, H.264, H.265)
  (1) waits for a missing packet at most `DEFAULT_MAX_GAP_WAIT`, 300 ms from the arrival of the
  first packet after it, then gives the gap up and raises `take_key_frame_request()` (it held
  a gap for `max_late` packets, which were 8.6 s at 100 kbit/s); (2) gives up everything
  before a complete key frame the moment the key frame is whole
  (`Depacketizer::is_key_frame_start`), with no request; and every builder (3) ignores a packet
  older than what it has already built or given up (it buffered it, where it looked like a new
  gap). An audio builder is otherwise unchanged. An application that drives the builder
  without a clock should call `pop(now)` at `poll_timeout()` and send a PLI when
  `take_key_frame_request()` says so. **Migration** (the old behaviour):
  `SampleBuilder::new(..).with_max_gap_wait(None).with_key_frame_release(false)`.
  `with_max_gap_wait` now takes `impl Into<Option<Duration>>`: a call with a `Duration`
  compiles as before. No RFC sets the bound; 300 ms is the value the capacity instrument
  measured best of 300, 600 and 1000 ms, and libwebrtc's receiver (3 s without a decodable
  frame, 200 ms while waiting for a key frame) is `rtci-video`'s `ReceiveConfig::chrome()`:
  `docs/receiver-gap-policy.md`.
  Performance: flush-2

- **interceptor, peer connection** (breaker-1): `DefaultInterceptorOptions` has two new public
  fields, `circuit_breaker` and `circuit_breaker_automatic_restart` (both `true`; see "Fixed"
  and "Added"). **Migration**: a struct literal adds them or builds on
  `..DefaultInterceptorOptions::default()`.
  `CircuitBreakerHandle::report_round_trip_time` now takes each round trip measurement as it
  is made and smooths them itself (RFC 8083 section 3); it used to store the value given.
  **Migration**: a caller that handed in an average hands in the samples.
  The RTP circuit breaker restarts a ceased flow by itself when the receiver's reports show
  the cause has gone (it never did). **Migration**: an application that wants every restart to
  be its own sets `circuit_breaker_automatic_restart: false`
  (`CircuitBreakerBuilder::with_automatic_restart(false)`).
  With the `Chrome` behaviour profile the default chain has no circuit breaker (`cb.enabled`).

- **ice** (`conf/ice-26-consent-late-responses`): `ice::AgentConfig` has a new public field,
  `consent_response_wait` (`ConsentResponseWait`, default `Rto`), and so has the setting
  engine's `ice` group. **Migration**: a struct literal of either adds `..Default::default()`
  or `consent_response_wait: ConsentResponseWait::Rto`. `stun::timer::RtoEstimator` is now
  `Copy` (an addition).
  Performance: ice-26-consent

- **turn, ice** (`conf/transport3-mays`): `turn::client::ClientConfig` has a new public field,
  `software_in_indications`, and `ice::agent::agent_config::AgentConfig` one,
  `new_tie_breaker_on_restart` (both off by default, see "Added"). A struct literal of either
  adds `..Default::default()` or the field set to `false`.
- **workspace**: this release is 0.2.0 (every crate, and every requirement on a workspace
  crate; `master` carried `0.2.0-dev` until the release): it takes changes that 0.1.0 users
  cannot take without a change of their own. Each such change is listed here. Git dependents
  that need the 0.1 API pin the tag `v0.1.0` or use the crates.io release.
- **interceptor** (fec-1): `StreamInfo` has a new public field, `fec_session` (ULPFEC in an RTP
  session of its own, see "Added"). A struct literal of `StreamInfo` adds `..Default::default()`
  or `fec_session: None`.
- **ice / peer connection** (`conf/ice-24-address-policy`): `AgentConfig` and the setting
  engine's `Candidates` have a new public field, `address_policy` (an `IceAddressPolicy`, see
  "Added"). A struct literal of either adds `..Default::default()` or
  `address_policy: IceAddressPolicy::default()` (which allows every address, as before).

- **ice / jsep** (mdns-5): new public fields `AgentConfig::multicast_dns_expose_known_public_addresses` and `AgentConfig::multicast_dns_expose_temporary_ipv6_addresses`, `MulticastDNS::expose_known_public_addresses` and `MulticastDNS::expose_temporary_ipv6_addresses` (see "Added"). Migration: a struct literal of `AgentConfig` or `MulticastDNS` adds `..Default::default()` (or the fields set to `false`).

- **rtci-sdp** (jsep-79, pass2): `MediaDescription::connection_information` is a
  `Vec<ConnectionInformation>`, every `c=` line of the media description in order (RFC 8866
  section 5.7: "Multiple addresses or "c=" lines MAY be specified on a per-media basis", for
  layered multicast). The parser kept only the last one. RFC8866-5.7-7 is `tested`
  (`grammar_test::several_connection_lines_in_a_media_description_are_all_kept`). Generated
  SDP is unchanged (one `c=` line per section).
  **Migration**: `connection_information: Some(c)` becomes `vec![c]`, `None` becomes
  `vec![]`; read `connection_information.first()` where one address was read, and
  `is_empty()` for `is_none()`.

- **interceptor** (rtp-1): `RtcpSessionEvent` has a new variant, `ReportingSsrc`, before
  `RoundTripTime`, so the implicit discriminants of the later variants moved
  (cargo-semver-checks `enum_no_repr_variant_discriminant_changed`). The enum is
  `#[non_exhaustive]` and its variants carry data, so no code could cast it with `as`; a `match`
  already needed a wildcard arm. Nothing to change in practice.

- **statistics** (vp-8r, `conf/vp-4-engine-boundary`): `DecoderStatsUpdate` has four new public
  fields (`jitter_buffer_delay`, `jitter_buffer_target_delay`, `jitter_buffer_minimum_delay`,
  `jitter_buffer_emitted_count`). A struct literal adds `..Default::default()`.
- **stream-driver**: `PeerDriverConfig` has a new public field `mdns_rate_limit` (`None`: the process's budget). Migration: a configuration written as a struct literal adds `mdns_rate_limit: None`, or builds on `..PeerDriverConfig::on(addresses)`.
- **stream-driver** (runtime-1): **the driver runs on an injected async runtime** (`runtime::Runtime`,
  an object-safe trait used as `Arc<dyn Runtime>`: spawn, the clock and timers, UDP sockets
  multicast included, TCP listen / connect, name resolution, `block_on`). It is given per driver
  (`StreamDriver::with_runtime`, `PeerDriver::with_runtime`); there is no global or default
  runtime. Built-in runtime types are features: `runtime-tokio` (default) gives `TokioRuntime`.
  Changes for users:
  - `StreamDriver::new`, `StreamDriver::default` and `PeerDriver::new` need `runtime-tokio`
    (on by default) and are otherwise unchanged. Migration: none with default features; with
    `default-features = false` add `features = ["runtime-tokio"]` or call `with_runtime`.
  - `sockets::bind_tcp_listener_in_range(ip, range, reuse)` takes the runtime first and returns
    `Arc<dyn runtime::AsyncTcpListener>`; `sockets::accept_by_ufrag(&listener, timeout)` is
    `accept_by_ufrag(runtime, listener, timeout)` over a `dyn AsyncTcpListener`;
    `SharedAccept::stream` is an `Arc<dyn runtime::AsyncTcpStream>`;
    `nat_mapping::map_port` takes the runtime first. Migration: pass `&TokioRuntime::new()` and
    make listeners with `runtime.listen_tcp(addr, false)`.
  - `dns-records` turns `runtime-tokio` on: the per-family and SRV / NAPTR lookups are
    `TokioRuntime`'s (`Runtime::resolve_family`, `Runtime::resolve_records`; another runtime
    answers the default: both families together, no records).
  - The datagram marking of ccrows-7 is the socket's (`runtime::Transmit::traffic_class`,
    `AsyncUdpSocket::unmarked`, `runtime::TrafficClassMarker`); `PeerDriver`'s counters are
    unchanged.
  - (runtime-2) With `default-features = false` the crate has no async runtime in its normal
    dependency tree (no tokio, mio, smol, async-io, hickory): CI checks it
    (`tests/dependency_tree.rs`, the `cargo.yml` step "Stream driver without a built-in
    runtime").
  - (runtime-3) `runtime-smol` gives `SmolRuntime` (smol's global executor, async-io's reactor
    and timers, smol's resolver). Several runtime features can be on at once; drivers on
    different runtimes live in one process (`tests/runtimes.rs`: a peer on tokio and a peer on
    smol connect and exchange data-channel messages).
  - (runtime-4) `examples/custom-runtime` (package `rtci-custom-runtime-example`, not
    published): `Runtime` implemented over async-executor and async-io, the driver with
    `default-features = false`; CI checks its tree has no tokio and runs it (two peer
    connections on it exchange data-channel messages). New public helpers for such runtimes:
    `runtime::{std_udp, std_multicast, std_tcp_listener, std_tcp_bound, std_tcp_connect_start,
    set_and_read_traffic_class, reset_on_close, TrafficClassMarker}`.
  - (runtime-5) `runtime-mock` gives `MockRuntime`: a virtual clock (`MockClock::advance`, and
    `MockRuntime::run` moves it to the next timer whenever nothing can run, panicking on a
    deadlock instead of hanging) and an in-memory network (`MockNet`: UDP, multicast and TCP
    between mock sockets; per-direction `LinkConfig` delay, seeded loss and blocking; a datagram
    filter; a log with each datagram's traffic class and fate; a host table). Two
    `PeerDriver`s connect on it with no socket and no wall time (`tests/virtual_time.rs`: a
    data-channel exchange over 20 ms links, ICE consent expiry after 30 s reported as failed,
    a lost DTLS ClientHello retransmitted after its timer).
- **stream-driver** (runtime-1, `conf/runtime-1-trait`, on master since train 25): **`StreamDriver`
  is no longer `Sync`, `Unpin`, `UnwindSafe` or `RefUnwindSafe`**, and `PeerDriver` no longer
  `Unpin`; `Accepted`, `SharedAccept` and `DriverInput` are no longer `UnwindSafe` /
  `RefUnwindSafe` (cargo-semver-checks `auto_trait_impl_removed` against v0.1.0). The driver
  holds the injected runtime and its tasks as trait objects (`Arc<dyn Runtime>`,
  `Box<dyn runtime::JoinHandle>`, which is `Send` but not `Sync`; TCP streams as
  `Arc<dyn runtime::AsyncTcpStream>`) and its input queue is an `async_channel` channel, whose
  receiver is not `Unpin`. `Send` is kept everywhere. Migration: share a driver across threads
  behind a `Mutex` (or keep it on one task and talk to it through its handles), pin it
  (`Box::pin` / `pin!`) where a future that owns it must be `Unpin`, and wrap it in
  `AssertUnwindSafe` for `catch_unwind`.
- **`StreamTransmit` has a new public field, `dscp`** (rtci-shared): the codepoint the driver
  sets on the TCP connection (RFC 8837 section 5: one per TCP connection, the highest-priority
  flow's). Code that builds a `StreamTransmit` with a struct literal adds `dscp: 0`.
- **ice / jsep / stream-driver** (mdns-4): new public fields `AgentConfig::multicast_dns_fail_closed` and `AgentConfig::multicast_dns_publishing`, `MulticastDNS::fail_closed` (the setting engine's mDNS settings) and `PeerDriverConfig::mdns_sockets` (see "Added"). Migration: a struct literal of `AgentConfig` or `MulticastDNS` adds `..Default::default()` (or `multicast_dns_fail_closed: false, multicast_dns_publishing: Default::default()` / `fail_closed: false`); one of `PeerDriverConfig` adds `mdns_sockets: true`, or builds on `..PeerDriverConfig::on(addresses)`.
- **stream-driver** (`conf/mdns-6-regression-test`): `runtime::Transmit` has a new public
  field, `source: Option<IpAddr>`, the address a datagram is to leave from (the engine names
  one for each mDNS datagram, RFC 6762 section 14). Migration: a struct literal of `Transmit`
  adds `source: None`; a third-party `AsyncUdpSocket` may ignore it where it sends from a bound
  address.
- **stream-driver** (`conf/mdns-7-per-interface`): `runtime::MulticastConfig` replaces
  `interface_v4: Ipv4Addr` and `interface_v6: u32` with `interfaces: Vec<IpAddr>` (one group
  membership per interface holding one of the addresses; empty: the default interface), and
  `MulticastConfig::mdns` takes them as a second argument. A runtime's `AsyncUdpSocket` is
  expected to honour `Transmit::source` for a multicast destination
  (`runtime::MulticastInterfaceSelector` does it for a socket with a descriptor).
  Migration: `MulticastConfig::mdns(group)` becomes `MulticastConfig::mdns(group, vec![])`;
  a literal sets `interfaces: vec![interface.into()]` for `interface_v4`, or the address of
  the interface for `interface_v6`; a third-party socket adds a `MulticastInterfaceSelector`
  and calls `apply` before each send.
- **stream-driver** (`conf/mdns-8-send-failures`): `<dyn AsyncUdpSocket>::try_send` returns
  `io::Result<usize>` (the system's error, `WouldBlock` when the socket cannot take the
  datagram now) instead of `bool`, and `runtime::mock::Fate` has a new variant, `SendError`.
  Migration: `socket.try_send(&t)` used as a `bool` becomes `socket.try_send(&t).is_ok()`; a
  `match` on `Fate` adds an arm for `Fate::SendError`.

### Behaviour changes

- **The session bandwidth an RTCP session measures counts UDP and IP** (RFC 3550 section 6.2:
  "Bandwidth calculations for control and data traffic include lower-layer transport and
  network protocols (e.g., UDP and IP)"). Where no `b=AS` / `b=TIAS` gives the session
  bandwidth, the session measures the RTP sent and received over the last two seconds; each
  packet now counts with 28 octets of UDP and IPv4, as the RTCP packets always did in the
  average packet size. Before, the RTP header and payload alone were counted, which
  understated the session (and so its 5 % of RTCP) by 28 octets a packet: 2 to 3 % beside
  video, a quarter for 20 ms Opus packets. Test
  `the_measured_session_bandwidth_counts_udp_and_ip`. Audit: RFC3550-6.2-1 (note).
- **`GccInterceptorBuilder` probes for bandwidth by default** (`with_bandwidth_probing(false)`
  turns it off). The pull-style GCC interceptor (a chain without a pacer) never probed: its
  estimate climbed from 300 kbit/s at 8% a second. It now sends the start-up clusters and the
  others the default interceptors send (RFC 8836 section 2, requirement 4, SHOULD), as bursts
  of padding on the RTX stream, when the chain has a NACK responder and RTX is negotiated;
  without them nothing changes. Probing asks for nothing above the estimator's own maximum
  (`BandwidthEstimator::max_bitrate`, new, default none).
  WHAT CHANGES FOR A CALL: a chain without a pacer now reaches the path's rate at the start
  (2.5 Mbit/s 0.5 s into the call, where it was at 1.4 Mbit/s after 20 s), and so meets a
  later capacity collapse from a higher rate, as a call through the default interceptors
  always has. Measured with the capacity instrument (200 calls a cell, the path drops from
  2.5 Mbit/s to 300 kbit/s for 20 s; train 32 round 3 with `conf/instrument-4`, hosted runs
  45568561644 / 45568566803 before, 45568576304 after, and round 4 with the sender's flush,
  45574610547 / 45574618542: the same figures to the digit), ParolNet's chain with the reference
  receiver (a gap given up after 300 ms, the default since the receiver's bounded wait): the
  three requirements are met before and after (a picture over 2 s old for more than 0.5 s,
  over 2 s without a new picture, over 1 s without audio: 0 of 200 calls each); the target
  under the cap 249 -> 229 kbit/s, retransmissions 67 -> 142 a call, audio packets lost 28 ->
  39, the oldest picture 1.09 -> 1.18 s; 1000 kbit/s is reached 17.5 s after the capacity
  returns (18.2 s before). With a receiver that waits without a bound in time the oldest
  picture is 7.9 s where it was 3.6 s: the repairs of a
  collapse from 2.5 Mbit/s take that much longer than from 1.4. Behind a short queue (100 ms
  at the capped rate) the repairs take about 12 s instead of 5.5 s and more than half of
  them are dropped at the queue again (263 retransmissions a call against 145), during
  which the encoder's target is at its floor: a known limit of a chain without a pacer at a
  collapse from full rate (nothing pauses or flushes; the NACK responder repairs in order).
  With both directions capped, 25 of 200 calls of ParolNet's chain show a picture over 2 s
  old for more than 0.5 s where 3 did (the same limit: the feedback path is capped too).
  One seeded call of `rtci-video/tests/receive_rtc2rtc.rs` rendered nothing for 1.13 s at
  such a collapse (bound 1 s): that file's calls keep a sender without probes, and the same
  call with the builder as it comes stands beside it as the ignored
  `known_limit_a_capacity_drop_from_the_paths_rate_leaves_no_long_freeze`
  (`docs/test-exclusions.md`), which fails until the limit is gone.
  (`conf/nack-11-decline-useless-repairs` removes the repair tail and the unbounded
  receiver's old picture named above, see "Breaking changes"; that one seeded call still
  renders nothing for 1.15 s with 2 retransmissions: the collapse itself, not the repairs.)
  THE WAY BACK: `GccInterceptorBuilder::with_bandwidth_probing(false)` gives the old start
  (8% a second) and the old figures.
  A chain without a pacer probes at the start and while the application sends less than the
  target allows, not after a large drop of the target (`ProbeController::set_unpaced`, set
  by the congestion controller when it measures a cluster that left as one burst): a burst
  is padding on top of the media into the queue that caused the drop, where a paced cluster
  is mostly the media itself (measured, same instrument: with such bursts 7 of 200 calls
  were over 2 s without a new picture against 3, and behind a 1000 ms queue the audio paused
  for over a second in 72 of 200 calls against 21). A chain with the pacer probes after a
  drop as before.

- **`cb.packet-size`, a governed behaviour: `BehaviourProfile::StrictRfc` takes RFC 8083
  section 3's packet size for the RTP circuit breaker** (`CircuitBreakerPacketSize::LastFrames`,
  the mean over the last 4 * G frames). `Rfc` (the default), `Chrome` and `Performance` keep
  the sending window's mean (libwebrtc has no RTP circuit breaker). Measured
  (`tests/circuit_breaker_reordering_rtc2rtc.rs::the_last_frames_packet_size_ceases_a_talking_call_the_default_keeps`
  and the sweep, hosted run 45409132256): a talking call over a jittered link is ceased with
  section 3's form in 14 of 24 cells (5 % loss: after 3.8 to 5.0 s), with the default in none.
  With breaker-1's rate-now rule (see "Fixed") section 3's form ceases that call in 5 of the
  test's 6 runs (after 3.6 to 31.6 s; hosted run 45521916073), the default still in none.
  Audit: RFC8083-3-3 is `setting` (measured); it was `partial`. Returned in
  `conf/ccrows-8r-cb-last-frames-test` after train 24 took it out: with the RTP/RTCP family
  (rtp-1, -2, -3, -5, -6, -8) its test, then one seed's first 15 s, saw no trip. The breaker
  read every report as before (each block matched to the flow, same report rate); the link's
  seeded loss is drawn per SRTP and SRTCP datagram, so the changed RTCP moved where the losses
  fell. The test now states the measurement's requirement: a 60 s call, seeds 11, 1 and 2 at
  40 and 100 ms jitter, ceased with section 3's s every time, never with the default (on the
  train's tree, seeds 1 to 10: ceased after 1.5 to 12.6 s, hosted run 45455917556).
- **jsep** (mdns-5): **servers given by `set_configuration` reach the engine's own STUN and TURN
  gathering** (W3C webrtc-pc "set the configuration": "Set the ICE Agent's ICE servers list to
  iceServers. As defined in [RFC9429], if a new list of servers replaces the ICE Agent's
  existing ICE servers list, no action will be taken until the next gathering phase"; RFC 9429
  section 4.1.18). They kept the servers the connection was built with. Now each ICE
  generation of each transport gathers from the list in force when it began: a generation
  already gathering keeps its list, the next one (an ICE restart, a new transport) asks the
  new STUN servers and allocates on the new TURN servers, and the allocations on servers that
  left the list are deleted then. Tests: `tests/srflx_gathering.rs::servers_set_by_set_configuration_are_asked_from_the_next_gathering_phase`,
  `tests/turn_udp.rs::turn_servers_set_by_set_configuration_are_allocated_on_from_the_next_gathering_phase`.
- **jsep** (mdns-5): **in mDNS `QueryAndGather`, a STUN answer equal to its base is a
  server-reflexive candidate** (draft-ietf-mmusic-mdns-ice-candidates section 3.1.2.2,
  MDNSICE-3.1.2.2-1: "a server-reflexive candidate will be generated; [...] and as such MUST
  NOT be considered redundant per the guidance in [RFC8445], Section 5.1.3"). The engine's STUN
  gathering dropped it as redundant with the host candidate, which in this mode carries only
  its `.local` name: a host with a public address offered no usable candidate to a peer that
  cannot resolve the name. It is now provided with raddr `0.0.0.0` / `::` and rport 9
  (MDNSICE-3.1.2.2-2), as libwebrtc keeps it under mDNS obfuscation
  (p2p/base/stun_port.cc, `UDPPort::OnStunBindingRequestSucceeded`). Other modes unchanged
  (redundant, dropped). Test: `tests/ice_mdns_exposure.rs::in_hiding_mode_a_stun_answer_equal_to_its_base_is_a_candidate_with_the_base_hidden`.
- **stream-driver** (mdns-4): with mDNS `QueryAndGather` the driver binds the host's mDNS sockets when its connection begins gathering, before the first host candidates (before: at the first mDNS datagram), and tells the connection for which address families it has none (`RTCPeerConnection::set_multicast_dns_publishing`). The names of host addresses of such a family are not registered: their candidates go out under a `.local` name that is not published (draft-ietf-mmusic-mdns-ice-candidates section 3.1.1), or not at all with `with_multicast_dns_fail_closed(true)`. Before, the name was registered and announced into a socket that did not exist.
- **ice** (mdns-4): a host candidate whose mDNS name cannot be registered keeps one unpublished name per address (its UDP and TCP candidates share it, section 3.1.1 steps 2 and 5); before, each candidate past the cap of 64 names got a name of its own. No `QueryAndGather` path writes the literal address any more except the fixed-IP mode's other addresses (the agent without an mDNS connection used to, a path that `Agent::new` never takes).
- **stream-driver**: **`PeerDriver` carries a connection's mDNS, within one process-wide budget** (draft-ietf-mmusic-mdns-ice-candidates section 7.1, MDNSICE-7.1-1). At the connection's first mDNS datagram the driver binds the host's mDNS sockets (port 5353, joined to 224.0.0.251 and, where the host has IPv6, ff02::fb), sends the engine's queries, probes and answers there and hands back what arrives; before, those datagrams were counted as unsent. Every mDNS datagram of every driver of the process takes one message from one `MdnsRateLimit` (`peer::process_mdns_rate_limit`, 40 at once then 10 a second); one the budget refuses waits, in order. `PeerDriver::mdns_datagrams_sent` counts them. `MdnsRateLimit::take` and `ready_at` are public.

- **video** (`conf/vp-9-no-keyframe-on-resume`): the send pipeline no longer forces a key
  frame when sending resumes after a pause (a target of 0 from the pacer). Nothing encoded is
  lost in a pause (the pacer keeps and sends what was written before it), so the receiver's
  references are intact; no RFC asks for a key frame there, libwebrtc encodes the next picture
  as it comes (`video/video_stream_encoder.cc` `OnBitrateUpdated`), and the engine's note on
  `RTCRtpSender::target_bitrates` says none is needed. A receiver that did lose something asks
  with a PLI or FIR, and the pacer's discards ask too; a request made during the pause is
  served by the first picture after it. `SendConfig::key_frame_on_resume` (default now
  `false`) keeps the forced key frame as an option; `SendConfig::chrome()` no longer sets it,
  since libwebrtc's form is the default. Tests:
  `a_pause_stops_the_encoder_and_the_resume_continues_with_delta_frames`,
  `with_key_frame_on_resume_the_first_picture_after_a_pause_is_a_key_frame`,
  `a_key_frame_asked_for_during_a_pause_is_the_first_picture_after_it` (a forced key frame by
  default fails the first and `the_chrome_profile_resumes_as_the_default_does`; hosted run
  45410448247), and in the capacity call
  `a_pacer_pause_stops_the_encoder_and_the_video_resumes_within_a_second` (there the receiver's
  requests during the long pause make a key frame due at the resume either way).

- **ice**: a TCP host candidate on a Teredo address (2001::/32) is ranked as the UDP-tunnelled
  candidate it is (RFC 6544 section 5.4): type preference 75 (section 4.2,
  `candidate::UDP_TUNNELLED_TYPE_PREFERENCE`) instead of the TCP host preference 125, so it
  comes after TCP host and server-reflexive candidates. New `candidate::is_teredo`. Conformance
  rows RFC6544-5.4-1 and RFC6544-4.2-2 are `tested`.
- **ice**: **a remote candidate whose address is an FQDN is ignored, not refused** (RFC 8839 section 5.1, draft-ietf-mmusic-mdns-ice-candidates sections 3.2.1 and 4; MDNSICE-3.2.1-1, MDNSICE-4-1). `add_remote_candidate` with such a line now returns `Ok` and the candidate reaches neither the agent nor the statistics, as a description's line already did; before, it failed with `ErrAddressParseFailed`. A `.local` name of more than one "." and a `.local` name on a non-host candidate count as FQDNs (only a host `<name>.local` is resolved by mDNS); in a description, the first used to reach the agent as an mDNS name and the second refused the description. A trickled line of an unknown transport or candidate type is ignored the same way.
- **rtci-dtls**: a resumption that carries no certificate where one should be is refused
  when a `verify_peer_certificate` check is configured (fails closed): a client fails a
  handshake that would resume such a ticket or session with `bad_certificate`, and a DTLS 1.3
  or 1.2 server that asks its clients for a certificate (any `ClientAuthType` but
  `NoClientCert`) resumes none (a full handshake runs, in which it asks again, with the
  normal check). Before, the check was skipped for an empty list. Two handshakes have no
  certificate by their nature and are not refused (`conf/dtls-resume-3`, after the second
  review): an **external PSK** handshake (RFC 8446 sections 2.2 and 4.2.11: it authenticates
  by possession of the key; the check is not called, as before), which the first form of
  this change failed for every configuration that had both external PSKs and a check (the
  server aborted with `bad_certificate`); and a resumption at a server with `NoClientCert`,
  whose first handshake had no client certificate to check either, which the first form
  silently turned into a full handshake every time. `ConfigBuilder::with_verify_peer_certificate`
  and `with_external_psks` now say what the check covers. Not reachable from the peer
  connection (its tickets always carry certificates, it configures no external PSK and its
  servers require a client certificate); reachable by other users of `rtci-dtls`. Tests:
  `dtls13/psk_test.rs::a_client_with_a_check_refuses_a_resumption_that_carries_no_certificate`,
  `a_server_that_asks_for_a_certificate_resumes_no_ticket_without_one_for_its_check`,
  `a_server_that_asks_for_no_certificate_resumes_with_a_check_configured`,
  `an_external_psk_handshake_completes_for_a_client_with_a_certificate_check`,
  `an_external_psk_handshake_completes_for_a_server_with_a_certificate_check`,
  `an_external_psk_handshake_completes_for_a_server_that_requires_client_certificates`,
  `resumption_test.rs::a_client_with_a_check_refuses_a_resumption_that_carries_no_certificate`,
  `a_server_that_asks_for_a_certificate_resumes_no_session_without_one_for_its_check`,
  `a_server_that_asks_for_no_certificate_resumes_with_a_check_configured`.

- **`rtci-stream-driver` marks what it sends (RFC 8835 section 4.2 SHOULD, RFC 8837).**
  `PeerDriver` sets `IP_TOS` / `IPV6_TCLASS` on its UDP socket before each datagram whose byte
  differs from the last (the new `RTCPeerConnection::traffic_class`: the RFC 8837 DSCP with the
  datagram's ECN bits), and `StreamDriver` sets each TCP connection's from
  `StreamTransmit::dscp`. Linux, macOS and the BSDs mark; Windows accepts `IP_TOS` and leaves the
  packets unmarked (marking there needs qWAVE or a Group Policy QoS rule; the driver uses
  neither). New: `sockets::set_traffic_class` / `traffic_class`,
  `PeerDriver::socket_traffic_class`, `PeerDriver::unmarked_sockets`,
  `StreamDriver::socket_traffic_class`.
- **A media flow whose DSCP the network blocks goes back to DSCP 0 (RFC 8835 section 4.2
  MAY).** Under the default `RTCDscpMarking::Rfc8837`, a flow sent with a codepoint other than
  DF that the peer's sender and receiver reports on its transport never name (three of them, at
  least two seconds after the flow began) is marked DF from then on, its RTX and FEC streams
  too; the other flows keep theirs. `RTCPeerConnection::dscp_blocked_flows` lists them.
  `SettingEngineBuilder::with_dscp_marking(RTCDscpMarking::WithoutFallback)` keeps marking,
  `RTCDscpMarking::Off` marks nothing. Nothing changes on a path that delivers the marked
  packets. Audit: RFC8835-4.2-2 `tested`; RFC8835-4.2-1, RFC8837-5-1 and 5-8 cite the driver.
- **interceptors (NACK responder, TWCC sender), repeat repairs follow the feedback**
  (`conf/rtx-1r-duplicate-repairs`): a request for a packet whose retransmission per-packet
  feedback reported received is no longer answered, and one whose retransmission left
  without a report yet waits for it: answered at once when the retransmission is reported
  lost, or when two round trips and the feedback interval (`REPAIR_REPORT_MARGIN`, 100 ms;
  1 s before a round trip is known) pass without a report; held requests keep their place
  and those behind them are served meanwhile. The receiver asks again every round trip while
  a packet is missing, and a retransmission can wait longer than that in the path's queue:
  after a sudden capacity drop 24 to 28 of 92 to 101 retransmissions (a chain without a
  pacer) and 35 to 41 of 90 to 103 (the default chain) repeated a packet whose first repair
  then arrived first (hosted traces 45341865225, 45342290711). The TWCC sender reports what
  transport-wide feedback says of each retransmission it numbered (`RetransmissionsReported`,
  new, on an empty RTCP carrier application-ward; keyed as `RetransmissionsLeft`); with RFC
  8888 feedback (the default between two endpoints of this engine) the responder reads the
  report on the RTX stream itself. Without per-packet feedback of either kind every request
  is answered as before. RFC 4588 section 7: the sender "MAY selectively retransmit only the
  packets that it deems important and ignore NACK messages for other packets"; RFC 8834
  section 6.1: "It is not appropriate to blindly retransmit RTP packets in response to a
  NACK": the sender's choice, bounded. Measured in `tests/capacity_cap_video_rtc2rtc.rs`
  (cap after 20 s, six seeds on three wall clocks, hosted run 45408404348; 0.1.0: run
  45407054812): without a pacer the oldest picture 2.90 to 3.15 s (4.35 to 4.51), 57 to 64
  retransmissions (89 to 97), longest freeze 1.28 to 1.29 s (1.28 to 1.32); the default chain
  4.14 to 7.13 s (5.56 to 10.23), 59 to 80 (90 to 104), 0.75 to 1.13 s (0.97 to 1.91), and the
  recovery's mean 15 to 25 s after the cap 898 to 2500 kbit/s (646 to 2500). After a 4 s
  outage and an ICE restart (six seeds) the chain without a pacer is frozen 0.33 to 0.92 s
  from one second after the switch (0.70 to 0.99), the default chain still shows no usable
  frame to the end of the run (a known limit of 0.1.0). The tests' bounds on the picture's
  age and the retransmissions on this branch are the tripwires of the perturbed ensemble
  (`conf/capmatrix-1-perturbed-ensemble`, measured on the tree before this change; this
  change sits well inside them). Not offered: libwebrtc's
  form (no resend within one round trip, `rtp_packet_history.cc` `VerifyRtt`) loses a repair
  (`vp8_nack_jitter_buffer_rtc2rtc::a_jitter_buffer_deeper_than_the_feedback_delay_repairs_
  every_detectable_loss` fails, hosted run 45346502179), and first repairs ahead of repeats
  (measured, run 45349364771: freezes of 1.62 to 2.39 s without a pacer, against 1.28 to
  1.29 s; the repeats left are repairs of lost repairs, which a receiver that plays in order
  waits for first). This narrows two known limits of 0.1.0 (the 1.4 Mbit/s cliff's cause (2),
  and the picture's age after a sudden drop with the pacer). Tests:
  `rtci-interceptor/tests/nack_repeat_repairs.rs`.
  **What is remembered of a repair is one packet's and ends by the clock**
  (`conf/rtx-1r2-duplicate-repairs`, after an independent review proved two defects in the
  first form, hosted run 45477234586: a "received" memory pruned only when another report
  came, so a request could be declined for ever and the packet that reused a 16-bit sequence
  number a cycle later was never retransmitted; and a transport-wide number kept for a
  retransmission by count only, so feedback on the packet that had the number a cycle later
  was taken for the old retransmission arriving). The responder keeps one record per packet
  for its latest retransmission (waiting in the pacer, left with no report yet, report
  overdue, reported received), named by the packet's place in the order the stream was
  written, which no later packet has again; a waiting request is for its packet too. Every
  state ends by the engine's clock at the request, write, notice or timeout at hand, whether
  or not another report or pacer notice ever comes: in the pacer 4 s, the wait for a report
  two round trips and 100 ms, a late report 4 s (`RETRANSMISSION_REPORT_HORIZON`), reported
  received 4 s (`DELIVERED_MEMORY`). A report counts once, for a retransmission of the packet
  held now: a report repeated (RFC 8888 reports a span of packets every time) does not extend
  the memory, one on nothing remembered begins none, the loss of an earlier copy does not end
  the wait for a later one. So a receiver whose feedback reports repairs it did not get stops
  the repairs of its own packet for 4 s per retransmission and no longer, and what is
  remembered is at most one record per place of the send buffer. The TWCC sender's number
  is a retransmission's until it is handed out again, until the numbering is half a cycle
  past it, and for 4 s. `RetransmissionsReported` names each retransmission with the instant
  it was made (`ReportedRetransmission`, new). Tests (the reviewer's three among them):
  sequence numbers and transport-wide numbers coming round at 100 000 packets a second,
  feedback and pacer notices that never come, a receiver that reports every repair received,
  feedback naming every number, requests and lost reports without end against the rate
  limit, and the sizes of what is remembered (`nack_repeat_repairs.rs`,
  `nack::responder::tests`, `twcc::sender::tests`); each rule has a mutation a test catches.
  Performance: rtx-1r2

- **interceptor** (fec-14): an audio packet rebuilt from a RED block (RFC 2198) takes the RFC
  6464 / RFC 6465 audio level extensions of the RED packet that carried it, as RFC 8854 section
  4.1 asks ("attempt to approximate this information"), where it had no header extension
  before; other extensions of the RED packet are still left out.

- **fec** (fec-12): a FEC session's m= section (RFC 5109 section 14.1, `add_fec_session`)
  states the per-packet congestion feedback the media sections state for the kind: the
  transport-wide sequence number extension (`a=extmap:1`, its own id in a section of its own)
  with `a=rtcp-fb:<pt> transport-cc`, and `a=rtcp-fb:<pt> ack ccfb` (RFC 8888), and an
  answerer keeps one of them (RFC 8888 section 6), RFC 8888 when both sides state it as for
  the media, the extension under the offer's id. The FEC session's packets then
  carry the transport-wide sequence number of their own transport and are reported on, so that
  transport's congestion controller (each transport is a path, RFC 8836 section 2) has the
  feedback it ran without before. A section without these lines (an earlier peer) is taken as
  before: no extension, no feedback.
- **congestion control (GCC), the over-use detector's threshold adapts over the arrival
  gaps** (`conf/gcc-9-draft-threshold-time-base`): draft-ietf-rmcat-gcc-02 section 5.4,
  `del_var_th(i) = del_var_th(i-1) + (t(i)-t(i-1)) * K(i) * (|m(i)|-del_var_th(i-1))`, t(i)
  the arrival time of group i, is now the default (`ThresholdTimeBase::Arrival`, for `Gcc`,
  `DefaultInterceptorOptions::gcc_threshold_time_base` and the `Rfc` profile row
  `gcc.threshold-time-base`). The earlier default, the gap between the readings on the
  sender's clock capped at 100 ms, stays as `ThresholdTimeBase::Departure` (a setting, no
  profile selects it); `Chrome` keeps libwebrtc's capped arrival gap (`ArrivalCapped`). It was
  kept as the default because it measured better; since the draft's decrease on every update
  (0.1.0) it no longer does. Measured (`rtci-interceptor/tests/rfc8836_multi_flow.rs`, hosted
  run 45416144506, against Departure): two flows on one bottleneck share 0.48 / 0.50 with a
  queueing delay of 2.9 ms mean and 11.0 ms p95 (0.49 / 0.49, 18.5 and 93.2 ms); a late flow
  0.49 (0.50); beside a TCP-like transfer 0.33 of the path with a 0.05 s buffer (0.25) and
  **0.14 with a 0.2 s buffer (0.22): the cost**, above the tests' bound of 0.05. The
  capacity-cap call (`tests/capacity_cap_video_rtc2rtc.rs`, six seeds on three wall clocks,
  hosted run 45416130268 against 0.1.0's 45407054812): without a pacer freeze, oldest picture
  and retransmissions unchanged, 249 to 281 kbit/s under the 300 kbit/s cap (246 to 252),
  1101 to 1501 kbit/s on average 15 to 25 s after it (1060 to 1363); with the pacer freeze
  0.97 to 1.87 s (0.97 to 1.91), oldest picture 6.01 to 9.83 s (5.56 to 10.23), 94 to 106
  retransmissions (90 to 104), 154 to 231 kbit/s under the cap (122 to 230), recovery 862 to
  2500 kbit/s (646 to 2500). The lossy reordering sweep (48 cells) is unchanged but for two
  cells of 100 ms reordering at 2 Mbit/s, higher (1 %: 331 -> 340 kbit/s, 5 %: 100 -> 218);
  the rate-limited link 574 / 539 / 535 kbit/s (574 / 538 / 535). Audit row GCC-5.4-4 is
  `tested`.
  Performance: gcc-9

- **media**: `H26xWriter` (H.264) gives the depacketizer each packet's sequence number, as it
  did for H.265: the fragments of a NAL unit after a lost one are dropped with it, not written
  as a NAL unit with a hole in it (RFC 6184 section 5.8). Conformance rows RFC6184-5.8-14,
  RFC7798-4.4.3-12 (`SampleBuilder` never depacketizes across a missing packet, now tested)
  and RFC7798-4.3-1 are `tested`.

- **jsep / sdp**: the `o=` line of a peer connection's descriptions is drawn once, when it is
  built (`conf/jsep-75-session-version`). The session version starts at a timestamp, the
  seconds since 1900 of the wall clock at that moment (RFC 8866 section 5.2: "it is RECOMMENDED
  that a timestamp be used"), instead of the clock's sub-second nanoseconds, and still goes up
  by one with each description that differs (RFC 9429 section 5.2.2). The session id comes from
  the crypto provider's `random()` and is below 2^63 - 1 (RFC 9429 section 5.2.1).
  `SessionDescription::new_jsep_session_description` writes the same kind of version. Peers
  see a larger first version (about 3.9e9, still below 2^32). Tests:
  `tests/jsep_session_version.rs::the_first_session_version_is_the_wall_clocks_seconds_since_1900`,
  `rtci-sdp` `grammar_test::the_jsep_templates_write_the_lines_rfc_9429_section_5_2_1_gives`.
  RFC8866-5.2-3 is `tested`.

- **jsep**: an offer with empty `a=group` lines (RFC 5888 section 9.3 capability indication)
  is answered with an empty `a=group` line for each semantics the engine understands and the
  answer does not use (BUNDLE, LS, DDP) (`conf/jsep-77-small-rows`). Offers without such lines,
  which is every browser's, are answered as before. Test:
  `tests/jsep_sweep_rfc5888.rs::empty_group_lines_of_an_offer_are_answered_with_this_endpoints_capabilities`.
- **jsep**: a section an answer rejects after writing it (outside the offered BUNDLE group
  under `must-bundle`, or beyond what the bundle policy takes from an offer without BUNDLE)
  no longer carries `a=candidate` / `a=end-of-candidates` (RFC 8839 section 4.2.1.6); the
  next section written takes them, and the local description puts the candidates in the first
  section that is not rejected (it used to be the first section) (`conf/jsep-77-small-rows`). Test:
  `tests/jsep_sdp_rows.rs::a_section_answered_with_port_zero_has_no_candidates`.
- **tests** (`conf/jsep-77-small-rows`): a late identification-tag does not end the session
  (RFC 9143 section 15,
  `tests/jsep_sweep_media_rtc2rtc.rs::a_late_identification_tag_does_not_end_the_session`); the
  end-of-gathering event names its section (RFC 9429 section 4.1.20). RFC9143-15-3, RFC5888-6-5,
  RFC8839-4.4.1.2.1-2, RFC9429-4.1.20-4, RFC3264-6.1-15 and 7-3 are `tested`, RFC3264-6.1-20 `n/a`.
  RFC5888-9.3-1 is `tested`; RFC8866-5.8-4 and 6.7.3-1 and RFC8122-7-1 gain the tests they
  lacked (`tests/jsep_sdp_rows.rs::bandwidth_lines_use_registered_modifiers_only`,
  `tests/jsep_sweep_media_rtc2rtc.rs::a_sendonly_endpoint_processes_the_rtcp_it_receives`,
  `rtci-dtls` `a_client_hello_offering_only_the_null_suite_is_refused`).

- **sdp / jsep**: a remote description with two direction attributes at one level is refused
  (RFC 8866 section 6.7: at most one at session level and one per media description); the
  first was taken before. The informational attributes `a=tool`, `a=type`, `a=orient` and
  `a=quality` (RFC 8866 sections 6.3, 6.9, 6.8, 6.14) now have their grammar checked, so a
  remote description with a malformed one, or one at the wrong level, is refused (RFC 9429
  section 5.8) (`conf/jsep-78-sdp-informational`). Browsers send neither.
- **rtp**: `Vp8Payloader` starts each partition of a VP8 frame in a packet of its own, with the
  partition's `PID` and `S` on its first packet (RFC 7741 sections 3, 4.2, 4.4): it reads the
  frame tag, the token partition count from the first partition's header (RFC 6386 section
  19.2) and the partition sizes. A frame with one token partition now goes out in at least two
  packets (the first partition, then the residual). A frame whose sizes do not add up is cut
  at MTU boundaries as before. `Vp8Payloader::ignore_partitions` (new public field) selects
  the old cut, which is libwebrtc's. Conformance rows RFC7741-4-1, 4.2-7, 4.2-11, 4.4-4 and
  4.4-6 are `tested`.
- **`vp8.ignore-partitions`, a governed behaviour: the `Chrome` profile packetizes VP8 as
  libwebrtc does** (`conf/vp-9r-vp8-partitions`). New `MediaEngine::set_vp8_ignore_partitions`
  (`false` by default, RFC 7741 section 3's partition packets; `true` under `Chrome`:
  libwebrtc's `RtpPacketizerVp8` cuts the whole frame, `S` on the first packet only, `PID` 0),
  `MediaEngine::payloader` and `RTCRtpSender::payloader(&codec)`, which build a payloader with
  the connection's packetization settings (`RTCRtpCodec::payloader` keeps the default form).
  `rtci-video`'s `VideoSender` takes its payloader from the sender, so its VP8 follows the
  profile. Tests: `tests/vp8_packetization_profile.rs`.

- **sdp**: an interleaved H.264 format (`packetization-mode=2`, registered by the
  application; no default format is one) is offered and answered with
  `deint-buf-cap=33554432`, the de-interleaving buffer the depacketizer holds
  (`MAX_DEINTERLEAVING_BYTES`), unless the application gave its own value (RFC 6184 section
  8.2.2). Default offers are unchanged.
- **rtp**: `rtp::codec::h264::mtap` writes its units in decoding order (ascending DON from the
  DON base), whatever order they are given in (RFC 6184 section 5.7.2). Conformance rows
  RFC6184-5.7.2-3, 7.2.1-1, 7.2.1-2 and 8.2.2-9 are `tested`.

- **RFC 8108 section 6.1: an endpoint starts sending on the SSRC it reported from.** A
  connection that sends no media reported from an SSRC its RTCP session drew, and when its
  first stream started (a receiver that turns `sendrecv`, an `addTrack` after the call is up)
  that SSRC said BYE and the stream joined as a second participant. The RTCP session now
  announces the reporting SSRC it draws (`RtcpSessionEvent::ReportingSsrc`, new; `None` once
  the SSRC is a stream's or said BYE); the first media SSRC the connection mints is that one,
  and the stream bound under it takes the reporting SSRC over: no BYE, one participant, its
  reports become sender reports. Later streams, and SSRCs the application
  names in a track's codings, are unchanged. On the wire: a peer sees RTP and sender reports
  arrive from the SSRC that sent the receiver reports (as libwebrtc does with its own
  receiver-report SSRC), signalled in the next description as usual. Engine behaviour change
  (SSRC handling). Rows: RFC8108-6.1-1 (`violated` -> `tested`).

- **RFC 4585 section 3.5.4: congestion control feedback sent at once counts in the average
  RTCP packet size.** The transport-wide and RFC 8888 feedback the RTCP session sends as it is
  built (`with_immediate_congestion_feedback`, the default) was left out of `avg_rtcp_size`
  when sent, though the peer's was counted when received; the clause has the average "updated
  accordingly" for every packet, Early or Regular. Now every packet sent moves it, so the
  regular report interval reflects the packets the endpoint actually sends (slightly longer
  where that feedback is larger than the regular reports). With
  `with_congestion_feedback_in_budget` (the `Performance` profile) the regular reports' budget
  still rests on their own size. Engine behaviour change (RTCP timing). Rows: RFC4585-3.5.4-2
  (`partial` -> `tested`).

- **RFC 8108 section 5.2: senders report first when not every SSRC fits.** When an endpoint's
  SSRCs cannot all report in one aggregated compound packet (the MTU), the RTCP session now
  puts the sending SSRCs' reports in first ("those most useful to the peers"), then the others
  by their timers; before, the order was the timers' alone. The SSRCs left out still report
  when their own timers expire. Engine behaviour change (report content on the wire, only for
  endpoints with more SSRCs than one packet holds). Rows: RFC8108-5.2-3 (`missing` ->
  `tested`); RFC8108-5.2-1 (initial report at zero delay, already done by
  `with_first_report_at_join`) marked `tested`.

- **RFC 7164: no RTCP timestamps around a possible leap second.** Taking up section 5.1's
  assumption of a positive leap second at the end of every month, the RTCP session sends no
  sender report and no XR receiver reference time stamped in the last second of a month's last
  day or the second after it (UTC): the SSRC reports with a receiver report there, keeping its
  schedule. A sender report received with such a timestamp is not used for LSR / DLSR or the
  remote-outbound timestamps (its counts are). New: `rtci_shared::time::near_leap_second`.
  Engine behaviour change (report content on the wire, two seconds a month). Rows:
  RFC7164-5.1-1 to 5.1-5 (`missing` -> `tested`), 5-3 (`missing` -> `partial`: the RFC 8888
  report timestamp and the NTP header extensions are still written there).

- **RFC 8108 section 5.1: the RFC form of `with_report_from_every_ssrc` reports on the
  co-located SSRCs too.** With `RtcpSessionBuilder::with_report_from_every_ssrc(true)`
  (`DefaultInterceptorOptions::rtcp_report_from_every_ssrc`, the `StrictRfc` profile) each
  local SSRC's SR or RR now also carries a block for each of the endpoint's other SSRCs that
  has sent ("including those co-located at the same endpoint": nothing lost, no jitter, the
  highest sequence number sent, that SSRC's last SR). The default stays `false` (blocks once,
  libwebrtc's form), measured: the RFC form's larger compound packets made the video freeze
  longer through a capacity cap (`measure_report_blocks_from_every_ssrc_against_once`: mean
  1.73 s against 1.60 s). No change with the default. Rows: RFC8108-5.1-1 (`partial` ->
  `setting`, measured).

- **rtp**: `HevcPayloader` puts the parameter sets, AUD and prefix SEI that precede a slice in
  the slice's aggregation packet when the slice does not fit the packet being filled and they
  fit one together, instead of leaving them with the units before them (RFC 7798 section 5).
  Conformance row RFC7798-5-5 is `tested`.

- **sdp**: an H.265 answer to an offer with `sprop-max-don-diff` above 0, and an H.265 format
  of this endpoint with it, state `depack-buf-cap=33554432`, the de-packetization buffer the
  depacketizer holds (`MAX_DEPACKETIZATION_BYTES`), unless the application gave one (RFC 7798
  section 7.2.2). Default offers, and answers to browsers' H.265 offers (which carry no
  `sprop-max-don-diff`), are unchanged. Conformance row RFC7798-7.2.2-10 is `tested`.
- **stream-driver, mdns** (`conf/mdns-7-per-interface`, review F1, F7, F8): `PeerDriver`
  took part in mDNS on the system's default multicast interface only, with one socket, and
  ignored the address the engine names for each mDNS datagram: names of addresses on any other
  interface (loopback included) never resolved, and every name was announced on the default
  link (RFC 6762 section 14: "addresses ... MUST be valid for use on the interface on which the
  response is being sent"). Now its mDNS sockets join the groups on the interface of every
  configured address, and each message leaves by the interface of its source
  (`IP_MULTICAST_IF` / `IPV6_MULTICAST_IF`, set per send by the tokio, smol and custom-runtime
  sockets, honoured by the mock); a query leaves once from each interface, on both families'
  groups. `rtci-mdns` names an IPv6 record's own address as the source of its messages (it named
  0.0.0.0), and the driver sends them on ff02::fb (and on 224.0.0.251 from the IPv4 address of
  the same interface, where it has one): an IPv6-only link gets mDNS, and the per-family
  publishing report (`set_multicast_dns_publishing`) says what is actually sent. Under
  `QueryAndGather` no two UDP sockets of a driver share a port (a `.local` candidate names its
  socket by port only); a range with no such port left falls back to a shared one. Tests:
  `mdns_virtual_time.rs::drivers_whose_link_is_not_the_default_multicast_interface_resolve_each_other`,
  `a_multi_homed_driver_answers_for_each_name_on_the_interface_of_its_address`,
  `a_publishing_driver_gives_each_of_its_sockets_a_port_of_its_own`,
  `mdns.rs::drivers_on_loopback_resolve_each_other_on_the_loopback_interface`. The mock
  network gives each address its own ephemeral ports and has a default multicast interface
  (`MockNet::set_default_multicast_interface`). Engine behaviour change (rtci-mdns: the source
  address of an IPv6 record's messages; IPv6 records of different addresses are no longer
  aggregated into one message, as IPv4 records already were not).
- **ice** (`conf/ice-25-mdns-tcp-candidate`, also in 0.1.0): a TCP host candidate whose
  address is an mDNS name was built as a UDP candidate (`CandidateHostConfig::new_candidate_host`
  gave every `.local` candidate `NetworkType::Udp4`), so the agent's own ICE-TCP candidates
  under `QueryAndGather` were signalled `… 1 udp … <uuid>.local 35225 typ host tcptype passive`
  and a peer's `tcp … .local` candidate was taken for UDP: two publishing peers had no ICE-TCP
  path. It now keeps its transport (RFC 6544 section 4.5; draft-ietf-mmusic-mdns-ice-candidates
  section 3.1.1 step 6 replaces only the address), and resolves to `Tcp4` / `Tcp6`. Tests
  `candidate_test.rs::test_tcp_host_candidate_under_an_mdns_name_is_signalled_as_tcp`,
  `to_json_of_a_tcp_candidate_under_an_mdns_name_says_tcp`. Engine behaviour change (SDP).
- **stream-driver** (`conf/mdns-8-send-failures`, review F2, F10, F11): where mDNS cannot be
  sent (the socket binds but every send to the group fails, as on GitHub's macOS image or in a
  Mac application without the Local Network permission), two publishing `PeerDriver`s sat in
  Connecting for ever and the application was told nothing; a bind failure was kept for the
  life of the connection. Now a refused send (at once for "no route" / "no permission", else
  after three in a row) or a failed bind is reported as `PeerDriverEvent::MdnsUnavailable`
  (`PeerDriver::poll_driver_event`, with the OS error), counted (`mdns_send_failures`,
  `mdns_bind_failures`, `mdns_available`), and fed to the connection as a family it cannot
  publish for (`set_multicast_dns_publishing`, so `with_multicast_dns_fail_closed` applies to
  the candidates gathered next); the socket is bound again at the next gathering and after a
  back-off (1 s doubling to 60 s), and the first send that works is reported as
  `PeerDriverEvent::MdnsAvailable`. What the mDNS sockets receive waits in a bounded queue
  (256, oldest dropped, `mdns_datagrams_dropped`). Tests `tests/mdns_failures.rs` (virtual
  time, every platform; the mock network refuses sends with `MockNet::set_send_error`) and
  `tests/mdns_unavailable.rs` (real network, `--ignored`, run on hosted runners). Not an engine
  change.
- **stream-driver** (`conf/mdns-9-shutdown`, review F3): mDNS goodbyes (RFC 6762 section
  10.1, TTL 0) left only when the application closed the connection and kept stepping the
  driver; dropping the driver sent none, and the link's caches held the names for 120 s. New
  `PeerDriver::shutdown(linger)`: closes the connection, sends every goodbye within the mDNS
  budget (waiting up to `linger`), then closes the driver's sockets, leaving the groups.
  Dropping a driver that was not shut down now closes its connection and sends at once what
  the budget lets go (an async driver on a pluggable runtime cannot wait in `drop`). Tests
  `tests/mdns_shutdown.rs`. Not an engine change.
- **mdns, ice, peer connection, stream-driver** (`conf/mdns-10-on-link`, review F6, F9, F12
  and its observation on peer-reflexive candidates):
  - RFC 6762 section 11's first test ("All responses received with a destination address in
    the IP header that is ... 224.0.0.251 or ... FF02::FB are necessarily deemed to have
    originated on the local link, regardless of source IP address") now applies through
    `handle_read` too: with the destination declared as reported
    (`with_multicast_dns_destination_reported`, new at run time
